queries.jsonl.gz.fields: id, corpus, doc_id, form, query, split

completions.jsonl.gz.fields: corpus, doc_id, ms, content (the raw completion), eval_count, done_reason, error, parse

prompt.template:
You write search queries for testing a document search engine.
Corpus: {description}
Document:
"""
{text}
"""
Write search queries that this document answers, as a person who has not seen the document would type them:
- {n} natural-language questions
- {n} keyword queries (3 to 8 words, no question words)
- {n} one-sentence statements of a fact that the document supports
Each query must be answerable from this document alone and specific enough to prefer it over similar documents. Do not copy a whole sentence from the document.
Reply with JSON only: {{"questions": [...], "keywords": [...], "statements": [...]}}

sample.reads: the fixture's files and each BEIR corpus.jsonl; never queries.jsonl or qrels

rule.equal: the normalised strings are the same
rule.normalise: lowercase, every run of characters outside a-z and 0-9 becomes one space
rule.cosine_of: unit embeddings of the bare queries
rule.dropped_when: any of the three holds against any test query of any of the three benchmarks

validation.rule: by source document, per corpus: the ids sorted, permuted (RandomState(seed)), the first max(min_documents, ceil(fraction * n)) are validation; every query of a document goes with it

what_this_is_not: no query has a relevance label; the documents are the benchmarks' own corpora, so a student trained on these queries has seen the documents its test questions are about, though no test question and no label
